**Summary:**  
The article argues that for cloud‑hosted workloads requiring high I/O throughput, Amazon’s EC2 i3 instance family (especially i3.large and larger) offers the best price‑to‑performance ratio because its built‑in NVMe SSDs deliver ultra‑fast, >1 GB/s storage speeds at competitive monthly costs. It presents head‑to‑head benchmark data (including price tables and network throughput tests) showing that while AWS’s “up to 10 Gb/s” network claims often fall short, the i3.xlarge is the only instance type with affordable NVMe storage and consistent performance. The piece is written as a practical, data‑driven tutorial aimed at system administrators, DevOps engineers, and developers evaluating cloud providers for storage‑intensive applications. It uses a straightforward “TL;DR” framing and occasional metaphor of “speed limits” to contrast advertised versus real network speeds.
